newsitem.title: USA: Mesh tubes hold promise for aneurysm treatment.
newsitem.headline: Mesh tubes hold promise for aneurysm treatment.

text.p: A Y-shaped wire mesh tube that is inserted into a bulging artery may be effective in treating some aneurysms, a team of European doctors reported in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine.

An aneurysm is a balloon-like expansion in a blood vessel caused by a weakened area of the wall of the artery. Repairing them often requires a complicated operation in which part of another blood vessel is stitched in.
The new research was an attempt to assess the alternative technique of inserting mesh-like tubes covered with polyester into the artery without resorting to major surgery.

Most tubes, known as stent grafts, are straight, but the research team led by Dr. Ulrich Blum of University Hospital in Freiburg, Germany, looked at Y-shaped tubes designed for the point where the body's largest blood vessel, the aorta, forks into two pieces.

Dr. Blum and his colleagues placed tubes from two manufacturers into 154 patients. The Y-shaped tubes were placed in 133 people while the remainder, whose aneurysms were not at the fork, got straight tubes.

The first-time success rate was 86 percent for patients who got the straight grafts and 87 percent for the volunteers who received the Y-shaped grafts. In cases where the first attempt to correctly position the graft failed, the surgeons tried again and were usually successful on the second attempt.
There were complications in only three patients and doctors then did traditional surgery to remove the aneurysm.
"With further refinement," the research team said, the tubes may become standard treatment for such aneurysms, "especially in patients at high surgical risk."
